hero: In a freestanding hemodialysis unit in Pampanga at night, a young Filipino physician on duty kneels beside a reclined dialysis chair counting the pulse of an older Filipina woman who looks pale and is sweating, while a nurse in scrubs attaches electrocardiogram leads and the dialysis machine screen glows beside them; rows of other chairs softly lit in the background, urgent but controlled mood, no text.

figures.teaches: Most falling pressures during dialysis are volume related and recover with first steps, but red flags demand a different path immediately.
figures.content: Top box 'Falling pressure or symptoms (yawning, cramps, dim vision)'. Step 1 'Lay back, legs up; stop ultrafiltration; keep blood pump running unless air, hemolysis, reaction or blood loss'. Step 2 'Recheck pressure; count pulse yourself'. Decision diamond 'Red flags? chest pain, breathlessness, irregular or very fast/slow pulse, altered consciousness, fever, bleeding, air or translucent cherry-red blood, more than one patient'. YES branch (red): 'ECG now; emergency protocol; call attending immediately; consider ending session'; sub-box 'Circuit cause (air, hemolysis, reaction, clotted circuit): clamp, stop pump, DO NOT return blood'. NO branch (green): 'Look for cause: weight gain, UF rate, meal, morning BP medicines, blood sugar'; 'No recovery: protocol fluid in measured portions'; 'Call attending; do not restart UF at old rate'. Footer strip: 'EBPG definition: SBP fall >=20 mm Hg or MAP >=10 with symptoms and intervention (opinion); nadir <90 mm Hg most associated with death (observational)'. '© renalcarematters.com' bottom right.

figures.teaches: Each circuit emergency has a recognizable clue, a first move, and a rule on whether the blood is returned.
figures.content: Five-row card, columns 'Event | Clue | First move | Return blood?'. Row 'Air embolism | foam in venous line, air alarm, cough, collapse | clamp venous line, stop pump, left side head down per protocol, oxygen | NO'. Row 'Hemolysis | translucent cherry-red blood, back or chest pain, more than one patient | stop pump, clamp, check other patients and water | NO'. Row 'Clotted circuit | rising pressures, dark streaks in dialyzer | replace circuit per protocol | NO'. Row 'Blood leak | blood-leak alarm, pink dialysate | stop, replace dialyzer | per protocol'. Row 'Needle out / line open | blood under blanket, falling pressure, alarm may not sound | stop pump, clamp, press site | only if circuit intact and sterile'. Small icon of a dialysis chair with an uncovered arm and the note 'Keep needle sites visible'. '© renalcarematters.com' bottom right.

card: An empty reclined dialysis chair beside a hemodialysis machine with its screen lit, a crash cart and defibrillator in the background, night lighting, no text.
